pageHelp: Swap firmware from the SD card. Put `.bin` files built for the Alchemy Lab bootloader in a folder named `alchemy` on the card. **File** picks one; **Flash** writes it, verifies it and reboots into it -- turn the pot down first, then all the way up. Picking the firmware that is already running changes nothing and does not reboot. **DFU** reboots into the bootloader's update mode the same way, for firmware without a picker of its own.

fields.name: Brightness
fields.help: Global LED brightness control in safe ranges. Uses more power.

fields.name: J7/J8
fields.help: **Outputs** (default): J7 and J8 are outputs 5 and 6. **CV in**: J7 and J8 become CV inputs A and B (±5 V) and outputs 5 and 6 go quiet. Hold B2: the middle-right pot picks what CV A moves and the bottom-left pot what CV B moves, on the output selected when you set it.

fields.name: USB port
fields.help: **Mac** (default): the front USB-C is HostLink over USB serial, for the web programmer, presets and the card. **Phone**: the front USB-C is USB MIDI, for the iPhone app (the panel's lights, the knobs, the buttons, the card and firmware switching). One setting for every firmware on the card. From the next power-up; hold B1 while powering up for Mac mode once.

storage.help: The SD card holds files the firmware reads and writes. Browse and manage them from the web programmer's file panel. Avoid removing the card while the module is writing; everything else is safe at any time.

manual.preamble: **Pulse** runs a master clock (10-300 BPM, tap tempo on B2, or follow a clock on J1) and eight outputs on J3-J10. Each output has a ratio (/64 to x32), a waveform (gate, trigger, saw, ramp, triangle, sine, envelope, stepped and smooth random), width, level, offset and phase; hold B3 for its euclidean pattern, chance, swing and slew. Tap B1 to step to the next output, or hold B1 and turn the top-left pot to pick one. Hold B2 for the tempo, the clock input's PPQN, what J2 does and where the CV inputs go. Tap B3 to start and stop. In Settings, J7 and J8 can become CV inputs A and B (outputs 5 and 6 then go quiet); on the B2 layer, the middle-right and bottom-left pots pick what each one moves on the output selected at the time.

presets.help: Preset slots store the complete state of the module — every page, every setting marked as preset material, and everything else the firmware manages. Slot 0 is the boot slot: it loads automatically at power-up. Presets are saved and named from the web programmer, or from the panel using the module's preset gestures. Slots written by a different firmware version are flagged in the programmer and can be migrated with **Back up all**.
